verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both claims concern bodyweight/body weight with TRE versus control. Side A (meta-analysis of 22 RCTs) reports a significant reduction in body weight with TRE (-0.48 kg, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.22, P<.01). Side B (RESET RCT) reports a per-protocol bodyweight difference of -0.4 kg (95% CI -1.8 to 1.0) after follow-up, and the authors explicitly conclude that '3 months of 10-h per-day TRE did not lead to clinically relevant effects on bodyweight' and that the per-protocol loss 'was not maintained after the 3-month follow-up period'. This is an explicit failure-to-confirm/no-clinically-relevant-effect conclusion against a reported significant effect, which takes the not_replicated branch even though the point estimates share the same sign. The extracted fields on both sides match their sources; the per-protocol follow-up estimate is the selected contrast on side B, and its assertion 'not_confirmed' is consistent with the source wording.

source_evidence.quote: body weight (-0.48 kg, 95% CI: -0.74, -0.22, P < .01) in the TRE intervention group were decreased to varying degrees compared with controls
this meta-analysis found a significant reduction in BMI, weight, and fasting glucose, as well as a rise in HDL-C level with TRE compared with control

In the per-protocol analysis, participants who completed the intervention in the TRE group lost 1·0 kg (-1·9 to -0·0; p=0·040) bodyweight compared with the control group after 3 months of intervention, which was not maintained after the 3-month follow-up period (-0·4 kg, -1·8 to 1·0).
3 months of 10-h per-day TRE did not lead to clinically relevant effects on bodyweight in middle-aged to older individuals at high risk of type 2 diabetes.

diagnostics.notes: Side B's primary ITT result at 3 months (-0.8 kg, p=0.099) also shows a same-sign nonsignificant estimate, but the selected claim targets the per-protocol follow-up contrast; the explicit no-clinically-relevant-effect conclusion in sentence 18 drives the not_replicated label.
